hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C+D)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C+\blueD A\cdot D$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of c squared and a length of c squared. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative ten c and the length is c squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of twenty five with a length of c squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{c^2}(c^2-10c+25)
\\\\
&=\goldE{c^2}(c^2)+\goldE{c^2}(-10c)+\goldE{c^2}(25)
\\\\
&=c^4-10c^3+25c^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Three rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of c squared and a length of c squared. Inside of this rectangle is c to the fourth power. At the rectangle in the middle, the width is negative ten c and the length is c squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative ten c cubed. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of twenty five with a length of c squared. Inside of this rectangle is twenty five c squared.

question.content:
